evals.prompt: Our Node API spends about 40% of CPU in buildReport() (report/report.mjs), called for every request, and --trace-gc shows scavenges all the time under load. report/replay.mjs replays the workload (`node report/replay.mjs`). Make buildReport cheaper and prove it. It must return exactly what it returns today for any input it accepts today, and throw where it throws today.
evals.expected_output: buildReport fused into one loop that preserves filter's truthiness and hole-skipping semantics and the reduce order, an oracle over empty, inactive-only, mixed, sparse, NaN/-0, and non-number totals, and allocation (--trace-gc counts, heapUsed deltas, or allocation profile) plus warmed-up timing numbers for baseline and candidate on node.

assertions.text: A check-owned oracle gets the same total (including -0, NaN, and string concatenation), count, key order, or thrown error type as the original for empty, inactive-only, mixed, truthy-flag, missing-total, sparse-array, and null-row inputs.
Over 50000 calls on 1000 rows, buildReport triggers at most a quarter of the original's scavenges (node --trace-gc, separate processes).

assertions: The reply reports allocation evidence (scavenge counts, heapUsed deltas, or an allocation profile) and warmed-up timings for baseline and candidate, with units, from runs it performed.
The reply states which runtimes were measured and that bun or browsers were not measured, unless it measured them.

evals.prompt: A teammate wants to replace every `str += piece` in our template renderer with `parts.push(piece); parts.join('')` because 'string concatenation is quadratic'. We run on Bun 1.4 and Node 26. Should we?
evals.expected_output: The agent explains V8 ConsString and JSC rope behavior with sources, does not endorse the rewrite by folklore, and proposes measuring both forms on both runtimes in separate processes before changing code.
assertions: The response states that += builds ropes (ConsString in V8, rope in JSC) and is not quadratic in those engines
The response cites a primary source such as V8 src/objects/string.h or a local %StringIsFlat / bun:jsc isRope probe
The response requires a measurement on both node and bun before accepting the rewrite
The response does not claim a speedup number that was not measured

evals.prompt: Speed up this Node service handler: `async function saveAll(items) { items.forEach(async (item) => { await db.insert(item); }); return { ok: true }; }`. Benchmarks show it returns in 0.1 ms.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies that the handler does not wait for the inserts, rejects the 0.1 ms benchmark as invalid, and replaces forEach(async) with awaited work (sequential for-of, Promise.all, or a bounded pool matching the database's limits), then measures the awaited operation.
assertions: The response states that forEach ignores the async callbacks' promises so the benchmark measures no work
The fix awaits every insert (for...of with await, Promise.all, or bounded concurrency)
The response considers the database concurrency limit before choosing unbounded Promise.all
Timing in the response covers the full awaited operation

evals.prompt: In our browser dashboard, `for (const el of cards) el.style.height = el.offsetWidth * 0.5 + 'px';` runs on every resize and Chrome DevTools shows 'Forced reflow' warnings. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The agent batches all offsetWidth reads before the writes (optionally scheduling the writes in requestAnimationFrame), checks that final styles are identical, and verifies with the DevTools Performance panel that forced reflows disappeared; it states that node/bun cannot verify this.
assertions: The fix reads every offsetWidth before writing any style
The response verifies identical final heights for all cards
Verification uses the browser (DevTools Performance or a headless browser run), not node
The response does not claim the fix was measured unless a browser run was performed

evals.prompt: Our Node image service computes a 400 ms perceptual hash per upload on the main thread, and health checks time out during bursts. Here is hash(buffer). Improve responsiveness.
evals.expected_output: The agent moves hashing to a worker_threads pool (or chunks with setImmediate if a worker is not acceptable), transfers the ArrayBuffer instead of copying when the caller no longer needs it, verifies identical hashes, and measures event-loop delay with monitorEventLoopDelay or timer ticks before and after.
assertions: The response uses worker_threads (preferably a pool) for the CPU-bound hash
The response addresses buffer ownership: transfer only when the sender does not reuse it
An oracle compares hashes from the worker and the original function
Event-loop delay or timer responsiveness is measured before and after

evals.prompt: Move our Express app in app/ from Node 20 to Bun: update package.json scripts and the Dockerfile. Don't run a Docker build.
evals.expected_output: The Dockerfile uses an oven/bun base image with bun install and a bun CMD, the scripts run bun, and no profiling or benchmark work is added.

assertions.text: app/Dockerfile uses an oven/bun base image and no longer runs npm or node, and the start script runs bun.
No CPU or heap profiles, benchmark files, mitata, or event-loop-delay instrumentation were added to app/.
assertions.check:
if find app -name '*.cpuprofile' -o -name '*.heapprofile' -o -name '*.heapsnapshot' -o -iname '*bench*' | grep -v node_modules | grep -q .; then echo 'FAIL: profile or benchmark files added'; exit 1; fi
if grep -rqE --exclude-dir=node_modules -e '--cpu-prof|--heap-prof|mitata|monitorEventLoopDelay' app; then echo 'FAIL: profiling code or flags added'; exit 1; fi
